name: Affinity Designer 2
note: Every row of Serif's "Keyboard shortcuts" page in the Affinity Designer 2 help. The context is the page's category with the trailing word "shortcuts" removed (Operations, File, Tools, Edit, Object control, Painting, Text, View, Selection, Workspace, Blend mode, Misc, macOS), plus the table's own qualifier where it has one, so the same tool name can appear under Tools (General and Designer Persona) and under Tools (Pixel Persona only). The page holds a Windows and a macOS variant of every row in the same HTML and picks one at load time; the web build's stylesheet only ever draws the macOS glyphs, so the Windows chords here are read from the Windows variant's own markup, in which Serif's Command tag is the Ctrl key. The page's "macOS shortcuts" table is emitted as macOS only, and the one row whose macOS form uses Control while sitting outside the per-platform markup (Delete from insertion point to end of paragraph) is treated as macOS only too; rows Serif gives only in the Windows variant (Home/End text navigation, Delete character to right of insertion point, Delete from insertion point to end of word) keep a Windows chord alone. Rows that document a set of keys - the arrow keys for nudging, [ and ] for stroke width - become one action per key with the chord repeated in parentheses. Left out because the chord grammar cannot express them: everything using a drag, a click, the mouse scroll wheel (view rotation, vertical and horizontal scrolling, the four Hot key zoom rows), Caps Lock, and the opacity/strength rows Serif writes as a run of numeric keys ("4=40%, 43=43%"). The whole "Shape Building" table is left out because Serif documents it on the numeric keypad only, as is the Fn-key row (Emoji & Symbols). "Setting brush properties on page" and "Setting brush hardness and flow" are sentences rather than chords. "Erase with Pixel Tool" and "Edit line or brush strokes as you draw/paint" are left out because Serif's markup prints a bare modifier with no key. "Justify Left" is left out because Serif writes its key as the pipe character, which the grammar has no spelling for. Where Serif writes the key as "+" (the macOS form of Zoom In) it is kept as Plus rather than guessed at.
